description: The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan Statistical Supplement reports insured populations, healthcare services and payments. Eight complete XLSX supplement descriptors cover fiscal 2014–2015 through 2021–2022. Sixty-four separately mapped packages explicitly identify themselves as tables from that annual supplement. Measures include practitioner headcounts/full-time equivalents, patients/services/payments by age, specialty, zone and recipient location, alternative payment arrangements, reciprocal services, registrants, fee changes, business-cost/rural payments, pharmacy counts, prescription coverage/costs, basic-service facility counts and Primary Care Networks. Further tables cover approved care unavailable in Alberta, out-of-province and out-of-country services, and top-50 health-service codes. The out-of-province package has an out-of-country URL slug; its title, description and descriptors establish out-of-province scope. The prescription measures concern delivered pharmacy services, not clinical drug effects. Distribution descriptors cover different annual and rolling windows within 2005–2022. Native dates can precede descriptor years; no continuous shared series, common population or numerical equivalence is asserted. The separate fee-for-service family retains its own named tables. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue preserves exact Alberta identifiers and full source descriptions. Sources state Open Government Licence - Alberta and unrestricted access, while isopen is false. Costs, current file access, precise table values and full annual coverage remain unverified. No workbook, report or dataset body was retrieved. Specific simulation applications are not stated. Related source tables retain distinct identities. Two further source-defined Statistical Supplement tables report total/average gross payments and service totals for physicians and allied practitioners by practitioner type. Their XLSX descriptors have different rolling windows within 2006–2022. These additions bring the mapped companion-table count to 64, alongside eight complete supplements. They retain the fee-for-service basis and are not interchangeable with alternative-payment measures.
